## Stage: RESULT

### Final natural-language hypothesis (data-grounded, descriptive)

Gardening and Unintentional introductions are positively associated with urban land use in the Barcelona study area, while AgriForest introductions are not; the urban effect is markedly stronger than the cropland effect and the modern temporal explosion of the Gardening pathway (about 22x since before 1500) is consistent with that link.

Expanded version, anchored on the data: Urban land use around sampled plots in Barcelona province (Catalonia) is positively associated with non-native plant introductions arriving through the Gardening and Unintentional pathways, whereas introductions through the AgriForest (agriculture and forestry) pathway show essentially no positive association with urban cover. Across all nine combinations of plot buffer (50 m, 500 m, 1000 m) and snapshot year (1956, 1993, 2009) in invaded_niche_pathways.csv, the per-row Spearman rank correlation between per-plot urban cover and per-plot pathway counts is rho about +0.24 to +0.40 for Gardening, rho about +0.27 to +0.50 for Unintentional, and rho about +0.08 to +0.11 (near zero) for AgriForest; the corresponding cropland correlations are weaker (rho about +0.10 to +0.27 for both Gardening and Unintentional), so the urban signal is clearly stronger than the agricultural one and is not a generic human-footprint artefact. A standardised per-plot logistic regression (n equals 632) on urban.2009.500m, cropland.2009.500m, elevation, temperature and road distance gives the urban coefficient +0.32 for Gardening incidence, +0.69 for Unintentional incidence, and -0.08 for AgriForest incidence; only the Gardening and Unintentional 95% confidence intervals exclude zero. Robustness on the 191 plots that actually carry neophytes, evaluated on row-normalised pathway fractions (separating composition from total introduction level), shrinks the per-pathway urban correlations to roughly plus or minus 0.13, indicating that urban cover mainly raises the number of introductions a plot receives while staying roughly neutral on the within-plot mix of pathways. The plot-level Urban habitat class itself (65 plots with mean urban.2009.500m about 0.57, about four times higher than Croplands' 0.13) accounts for 151 of the 481 active species occurrences, of which 69 percent are Unintentional, 30 percent Gardening and only 1 percent AgriForest. As an independent temporal line of evidence, temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv (1046 introductions across 4 historical periods by 3 pathways) shows the Gardening pathway rising about 22-fold from 18 introductions in the pre-1500 period to 397 in 1985-2019, the Unintentional pathway rising about 2.9-fold from 34 to 99, and AgriForest declining from 55 to 32 (about 0.58x); the pathway that bursts in the modern era (Gardening) is mechanistically the one tied to urban ornamental and horticultural trade, independent corroboration of the plot-level urban association. The findings are descriptive: the dataset is correlational, plots are clustered within habitats and are spatially autocorrelated, so no causal claim beyond the regression and Spearman magnitudes is asserted.

### Workflow executed

Loaded all four assets with the correct separator (temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv and invaded_niche_pathways.csv are tab-separated with quoted headers and were re-read with sep equals tab; invasion_success_pathways.csv and phylogenetic_tree.txt were loaded with default parsers). Sanity-checked the row identity that n.gard plus n.unint plus n.agfo equals n.total on all 632 rows of invaded_niche_pathways.csv (max absolute diff equals 0). Confirmed the introduction.period by pathway by n structure in temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv (12 rows, 4 periods by 3 pathways, sum n equals 1046). Verified that all 81 Newick tip labels reconcile one-to-one with phylo.tip.label in invasion_success_pathways.csv. Computed per-row Spearman correlations between every pathway-count and every urban cover variable, plus the cropland analogues and the change-proportion variables. Restricted the analysis to the 191 active rows and re-ran Spearman on the row-normalised fractions as a composition-versus-level robustness check. Fit per-pathway logistic regression at the plot level (n equals 632) on standardised versions of urban.2009.500m, cropland.2009.500m, elevation, annual.temperature, distance.road. Aggregated n.gard, n.unint, n.agfo and mean urban.2009.500m per habitat class across 10 categories and inspected the Urban stratum. Pivoted temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv (pathway by period) and computed the modern over pre-1500 ratio per pathway; Gardening ratio about 22x, AgriForest ratio about 0.58x. Did not use the phylogenetic tree for the urban hypothesis because the urban buffer data are plot-level, not species-level. Numeric outputs saved to analysis_results.json.

### Numeric anchors

Plot-level Spearman rho at urban.2009.500m: n.gard +0.395, n.unint +0.497, n.agfo +0.113, n.total +0.548. Cropland analogues: n.gard +0.096, n.unint +0.193, n.agfo +0.068 (all smaller than the urban rho). Urban minus cropland rho-difference at 2009 / 500 m: Gardening +0.299, Unintentional +0.304, AgriForest +0.045. Active-row Spearman at urban.2009.500m on fractions p_k: p_gard -0.106, p_unint +0.137, p_agfo -0.132 (small effects; level effect dominates). Logistic regression on Pr(n.k above 0) at plot level gives urban coefficient for Gardening +0.316, Unintentional +0.686, AgriForest -0.078; only Gardening and Unintentional confidence intervals exclude zero. Urban habitat class: 65 plots, mean urban.2009.500m equals 0.566, 151 species occurrences (30 percent Gardening, 69 percent Unintentional, 1 percent AgriForest). Croplands habitat class: 92 plots, mean urban.2009.500m equals 0.133, mean cropland.2009.500m equals 0.445, 108 species occurrences. Temporal trajectory (Before 1500 to 1985-2019): Gardening 18 to 397 (22.1x), Unintentional 34 to 99 (2.91x), AgriForest 55 to 32 (0.58x).

### Files produced

run_analysis.py (main executed script), run_glm.py (logistic regression script), inspect_datasets.py and inspect_more.py and final_capture.py (inspection and extraction scripts), analysis_results.json (full numeric outputs), analysis_run.log (captured stdout).
